concepts.name: Types of number
concepts.description: Natural numbers, integers (positive, zero and negative), even, odd and prime numbers, square and cube numbers, rational and irrational numbers (recognising numbers such as √2 and π as irrational), reciprocals, and writing numbers in words and figures.

concepts.name: Factors, multiples, HCF and LCM
concepts.description: Factors and multiples, prime factorisation (as a product of primes and in index form), the highest common factor and lowest common multiple of two or three numbers, and problems that use them, such as when two repeating events next coincide.

concepts.name: Set language and notation
concepts.description: Describing sets by listing, in words and in set-builder notation; elements and n(A); the universal set, the empty set, complement, subsets, union and intersection. (Cambridge 2025 no longer uses proper-subset notation; ZIMSEC does.)

concepts.name: Venn diagrams
concepts.description: Representing sets in Venn diagrams with two sets (Cambridge Core) or up to three sets (Cambridge Extended, ZIMSEC), describing shaded regions in set notation, and finding numbers of elements, including forming and solving an equation from the information given.

concepts.name: Powers and roots
concepts.description: Squares, square roots, cubes, cube roots and other powers and roots of numbers, with and without a calculator; recall of the squares of 1 to 15 and the cubes of 1 to 5 and 10 (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Fractions, decimals and percentages
concepts.description: Proper and improper fractions and mixed numbers, equivalent fractions and simplest form, converting between fractions, decimals and percentages, and (Cambridge Extended) recurring-decimal notation and converting recurring decimals to fractions.

concepts.name: Ordering quantities
concepts.description: Ordering numbers and quantities given in different forms (fractions, decimals, percentages, negative numbers) by size and using =, ≠, >, <, ≥ and ≤.

concepts.name: The four operations
concepts.description: Non-calculator methods for adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing integers, fractions, mixed numbers and decimals; directed (negative) numbers in contexts such as temperature; the order of operations including brackets.

concepts.name: Indices with numbers
concepts.description: Evaluating numbers with positive, zero and negative integer indices and (Cambridge Extended, ZIMSEC) fractional indices, and the rules of indices applied to numbers, without a calculator.

concepts.name: Standard form
concepts.description: Writing numbers as A × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ A < 10 and n an integer, converting to and from ordinary numbers, and calculating with numbers in standard form with and without a calculator.

concepts.name: Estimation and rounding
concepts.description: Rounding to decimal places, significant figures and the nearest 10, 100 or 1000; estimating calculations by rounding each number to one significant figure; choosing a sensible accuracy for an answer in context.

concepts.name: Limits of accuracy
concepts.description: Upper and lower bounds of values rounded to a given accuracy, and (Cambridge Extended, ZIMSEC simple cases) the bounds of sums, differences, products and quotients of rounded values, such as the greatest possible area or the least possible speed.

concepts.name: Ratio and proportion
concepts.description: Simplifying ratios (including ratios of three quantities and in the form 1 : n), sharing a quantity in a given ratio, the unitary method, direct and inverse proportion in context (recipes, best value, workers and time).

concepts.name: Rates and compound measures
concepts.description: Average speed, distance and time; density, pressure and population density from given formulas; rates of pay, flow rates and fuel consumption; converting compound units such as km/h to m/s.

concepts.name: Percentages
concepts.description: A percentage of a quantity, one quantity as a percentage of another, percentage increase and decrease using multipliers, percentage change, percentages over 100%, repeated percentage change and (Cambridge Extended) reverse percentages.

concepts.name: Simple and compound interest
concepts.description: Simple interest (I = PRT/100) and compound interest by repeated multiplication, finding the amount, the interest, the principal, the rate or the time, and comparing savings and loan options. Cambridge papers give no interest formulas.

concepts.name: Profit, loss, discount, commission and hire purchase
concepts.description: Cost price and selling price, profit and loss as amounts and as percentages, discounts, commission on sales, deposits, and hire purchase (instalment) prices compared with cash prices.

concepts.name: Household and personal finance
concepts.description: Wages and salaries (hourly pay, overtime, piece work), household budgets, electricity and water bills with fixed charges and tariffs, bank statements and balances, and insurance premiums.

concepts.name: Taxes and duties
concepts.description: Income tax (PAYE) from given tax bands and allowances, sales tax and value added tax (VAT), and customs and excise duty calculated from given rates (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Money and foreign exchange
concepts.description: Calculating with money and converting between currencies (US dollars, ZiG, South African rand, pounds and others) using given exchange rates, including buying and selling rates.

concepts.name: Exponential growth and decay
concepts.description: Repeated percentage change as a multiplier raised to a power: depreciation, appreciation and population growth or decay; finding the value after n periods and the number of periods needed to pass a target.

concepts.name: Surds
concepts.description: Simplifying surds such as √20 = 2√5, adding, subtracting, multiplying and expanding expressions with surds, and rationalising denominators such as a/√b and a/(b + √c) (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Number bases
concepts.description: Place value in bases two to ten, converting between base ten and other bases and between two non-denary bases, adding and subtracting in bases other than ten, and finding an unknown base (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Time
concepts.description: Units of time and conversions between them, the 12-hour and 24-hour clocks, time intervals, timetables, time zones and time differences.

concepts.name: Using a calculator
concepts.description: Using a scientific calculator efficiently: entering fractions, powers and times correctly, keeping full accuracy until the final answer, and interpreting the display in context (for example 4.8 as 4 dollars 80 cents, 3.25 hours as 3 hours 15 minutes) (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Algebraic expressions and substitution
concepts.description: Using letters for unknown and general numbers, writing expressions and formulas from words, collecting like terms, and substituting values (including negative numbers and fractions) into expressions and formulas.

concepts.name: Expanding brackets
concepts.description: Expanding a single bracket, the product of two binomials, perfect squares such as (x + a)² and (Cambridge Extended) products of three brackets, then simplifying.

concepts.name: Factorising algebraic expressions
concepts.description: Factorising fully by a common factor, by grouping, as a difference of two squares, as a perfect square and as a quadratic trinomial (including ax² + bx + c with a ≠ 1, and ax³ + bx² + cx for Cambridge Extended), checking by expanding. The key is historical: expanding brackets is the separate concept math.algebra.expanding-brackets.

concepts.name: Algebraic fractions
concepts.description: The HCF and LCM of algebraic expressions, simplifying algebraic fractions by factorising, and adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing algebraic fractions.

concepts.name: Laws of indices in algebra
concepts.description: Using the laws of indices with algebraic terms, including zero, negative and fractional indices, and solving simple equations with the unknown in the index, such as 2ˣ = 32 or 9ˣ = 27.

concepts.name: Logarithms
concepts.description: The relationship between indices and logarithms, the laws of logarithms (product, quotient and power), evaluating and simplifying logarithmic expressions, and solving simple equations with logarithms (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Linear equations
concepts.description: Forming and solving linear equations in one unknown, including equations with brackets, unknowns on both sides, and fractions with numerical or (Cambridge Extended) linear algebraic denominators.

concepts.name: Simultaneous linear equations
concepts.description: Forming and solving a pair of simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns by elimination and by substitution, and interpreting the solution as the point where two straight lines meet.

concepts.name: Simultaneous equations with one non-linear equation
concepts.description: Solving a linear equation together with a quadratic equation (such as y = x² + 2x − 3 or xy = 6) by substitution, and interpreting the solutions as the intersection points of a line and a curve (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Changing the subject of a formula
concepts.description: Rearranging formulas, including those with brackets, fractions, squares and square roots of the subject, and (Cambridge Extended) formulas where the subject appears twice.

concepts.name: Solving quadratic equations by factorising
concepts.description: Rearranging to ax^2 + bx + c = 0, factorising and using the zero-product property, including equations with no constant term and differences of two squares.

concepts.name: Completing the square
concepts.description: Writing ax^2 + bx + c in the form a(x + p)^2 + q, solving equations by completing the square and finding turning points.

concepts.name: The quadratic formula and the discriminant
concepts.description: Solving ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with the quadratic formula to a required accuracy, and using b^2 - 4ac to decide the number of real roots.

concepts.name: Problems leading to quadratic equations
concepts.description: Forming quadratic equations from area, number, speed and projectile contexts, solving them and rejecting impossible solutions.

concepts.name: Linear inequalities
concepts.description: Inequality symbols, showing inequalities on a number line with open and closed circles, solving linear inequalities and double inequalities such as −3 ≤ 3x − 2 < 7, and listing integer solutions.

concepts.name: Inequalities in two variables
concepts.description: Showing linear inequalities in two variables as regions on a graph (broken lines for strict and solid lines for inclusive inequalities, shading the unwanted region unless told otherwise) and writing down the inequalities that define a given region.

concepts.name: Linear programming
concepts.description: Forming inequalities from a practical problem, drawing the feasible region, and finding the maximum or minimum value of a quantity such as profit or cost at the vertices or by a search line (ZIMSEC; not in Cambridge IGCSE).

concepts.name: Sequences and number patterns
concepts.description: Continuing number sequences and patterns, term-to-term rules, relationships between sequences, and finding and using the nth term of a linear sequence.

concepts.name: nth term of non-linear sequences
concepts.description: Finding and using the nth term of quadratic and simple cubic sequences (Cambridge Core: simple cases such as n² + 1) and of exponential sequences and simple combinations (Cambridge Extended), including subscript notation such as uₙ.

concepts.name: Direct and inverse variation
concepts.description: Direct and inverse variation (proportion) with x, x², x³, √x and ∛x; using the ∝ symbol, finding the constant of variation and unknown values, and recognising the graphs of direct and inverse variation.

concepts.name: Joint and partial variation
concepts.description: Joint variation (for example z varies as x and inversely as y²) and partial variation (for example y = kx + c), finding the constants from given values and solving problems (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Function notation
concepts.description: Function notation f(x), evaluating functions, solving f(x) = k, mapping diagrams, and the meaning of the domain and range of a function.

concepts.name: Inverse and composite functions
concepts.description: Finding inverse functions f⁻¹(x), forming composite functions such as fg(x) = f(g(x)), and solving equations that involve them (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Graphs in practical situations
concepts.description: Conversion graphs and other real-life graphs: drawing them from data, reading values from them, and interpreting the gradient of a straight-line graph as a rate of change.

concepts.name: Travel graphs
concepts.description: Distance–time and speed–time graphs: drawing and reading journeys, speed as the gradient of a distance–time graph, acceleration and deceleration from a speed–time graph, and distance as the area under a speed–time graph.

concepts.name: Graphs of functions
concepts.description: Tables of values and graphs of linear, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal and exponential functions; reading values and turning points from graphs; solving equations graphically, including drawing a suitable straight line to find intersections.

concepts.name: Gradient of a curve
concepts.description: Estimating the gradient of a curve at a point by drawing a tangent, and interpreting it as a rate of change, such as speed from a distance–time curve.

concepts.name: Sketching curves
concepts.description: Recognising and sketching linear, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal and exponential graphs, showing intercepts, roots, symmetry, turning points and asymptotes (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Differentiation
concepts.description: Differentiating axⁿ (n a positive integer or zero) and sums of such terms, using dy/dx to find gradients of curves and stationary points, and deciding whether a turning point is a maximum or a minimum (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Coordinates
concepts.description: Plotting and reading points in all four quadrants of a Cartesian grid.

concepts.name: Drawing straight-line graphs
concepts.description: Tables of values and straight-line graphs from equations such as y = 2x − 3, x = 4 and x + 2y = 6.

concepts.name: Gradient of a straight line
concepts.description: Finding gradients of straight lines from a grid and from the coordinates of two points, and interpreting positive, negative, zero and undefined gradients.

concepts.name: Length and midpoint of a line segment
concepts.description: The length of a line segment and the coordinates of its midpoint from the coordinates of its end points (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Equation of a straight line
concepts.description: Interpreting and finding the equation of a straight line in the forms y = mx + c and ax + by = c, from a graph, from a point and the gradient, or from two points.

concepts.name: Parallel lines
concepts.description: Parallel lines have equal gradients; finding the equation of a line parallel to a given line through a given point.

concepts.name: Perpendicular lines
concepts.description: Gradients of perpendicular lines multiply to −1; equations of perpendicular lines and perpendicular bisectors (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Geometrical terms and vocabulary
concepts.description: Points, lines and planes, parallel and perpendicular lines, types of angle (acute, right, obtuse, reflex, complementary, supplementary), the vocabulary of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, circles, solids and nets, and the meaning of similar, congruent and scale factor.

concepts.name: Angle properties
concepts.description: Angles at a point and on a straight line, vertically opposite angles, corresponding, alternate and co-interior angles with parallel lines, angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals, three-letter angle notation and giving geometric reasons.

concepts.name: Polygons
concepts.description: Properties of triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons, names of polygons up to ten sides, interior and exterior angle sums, and finding the number of sides of a regular polygon.

concepts.name: Geometrical constructions
concepts.description: Measuring and drawing lines and angles, constructing triangles and quadrilaterals with a ruler and compasses (showing arcs), nets of solids, and (ZIMSEC) constructing perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors, perpendiculars and angles of 60°, 30°, 90° and 45°.

concepts.name: Loci
concepts.description: Loci of points at a fixed distance from a point or a line and equidistant from two points or two intersecting lines, and regions defined by intersecting loci (ZIMSEC; not in Cambridge IGCSE).

concepts.name: Scale drawings and map scales
concepts.description: Scales written as ratios and representative fractions, finding actual distances and areas from maps and plans (area scale = square of the length scale), and making and interpreting scale drawings.

concepts.name: Bearings
concepts.description: Three-figure bearings measured clockwise from north, compass bearings such as N 40° E (ZIMSEC), the bearing of A from B given the bearing of B from A, and solving bearing problems by scale drawing or calculation.

concepts.name: Similarity
concepts.description: Similar figures and the length scale factor, showing that two triangles are similar, and the area and volume factors k² and k³ for similar shapes and solids (including masses of similar solids for ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Congruent triangles
concepts.description: Congruent figures, the conditions for congruent triangles (SSS, SAS, ASA or AAS, RHS), and using congruence to find lengths and angles (ZIMSEC; Cambridge only uses the term).

concepts.name: Symmetry
concepts.description: Line symmetry and order of rotational symmetry of plane shapes, properties of triangles, quadrilaterals and regular polygons related to their symmetry, and (Cambridge Extended) planes and axes of symmetry of solids.

concepts.name: Angle properties of circles
concepts.description: Angle in a semicircle, tangent and radius, angle at the centre, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals and the alternate segment theorem.

concepts.name: Symmetry properties of chords and tangents
concepts.description: Equal chords are equidistant from the centre, the perpendicular bisector of a chord passes through the centre, tangents from an external point are equal.

concepts.name: Units of measure
concepts.description: Metric units of length, mass, capacity, area and volume, converting between them (including cm² to m², cm³ to litres and the hectare), and choosing suitable units.

concepts.name: Area and perimeter
concepts.description: Perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms and trapezia, including finding a missing length from the area.

concepts.name: Circles, arcs and sectors
concepts.description: Circumference and area of a circle, arc length and sector area as fractions of the circle (minor and major), answers in terms of π, and the area of a segment.

concepts.name: Surface area and volume of prisms and cylinders
concepts.description: Surface area and volume of cuboids, prisms of any uniform cross-section and cylinders, including capacity and problems such as filling a tank.

concepts.name: Surface area and volume of pyramids, cones and spheres
concepts.description: Surface area and volume of pyramids, cones, spheres and hemispheres using the given formulas, including the slant height of a cone.

concepts.name: Compound shapes
concepts.description: Perimeters, areas, surface areas and volumes of compound shapes and solids and of parts of shapes, such as hemispheres and frustums.

concepts.name: Pythagoras' theorem
concepts.description: Using Pythagoras' theorem to find sides of right-angled triangles, Pythagorean triples, and testing whether a triangle is right-angled, including in context.

concepts.name: Trigonometry in right-angled triangles
concepts.description: Sine, cosine and tangent ratios of acute angles to find sides and angles in right-angled triangles, two-dimensional problems including bearings, and the perpendicular as the shortest distance from a point to a line.

concepts.name: Angles of elevation and depression
concepts.description: Identifying angles of elevation and depression and using them with trigonometry or scale drawing to find heights and distances.

concepts.name: Exact trigonometric values
concepts.description: Exact values of sine and cosine of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60° and 90° and of tangent of 0°, 30°, 45° and 60° (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Trigonometric ratios of obtuse angles
concepts.description: Sine, cosine and tangent of angles between 90° and 180°, including sin(180° − θ) = sin θ and cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ, as used with the sine and cosine rules.

concepts.name: Trigonometric functions
concepts.description: Graphs of y = sin x, y = cos x and y = tan x for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360° and solving simple trigonometric equations in that interval (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Sine and cosine rules
concepts.description: The sine rule, the cosine rule and the area formula ½ab sin C for any triangle, including obtuse angles, the ambiguous case and bearing problems.

concepts.name: Trigonometry in three dimensions
concepts.description: Lengths and angles in three-dimensional shapes such as cuboids and pyramids using Pythagoras' theorem and trigonometry, including the angle between a line and a plane.

concepts.name: Reflection, rotation and translation
concepts.description: Drawing and fully describing reflections in lines (including x = a, y = b, y = x and y = −x), rotations about a centre through multiples of 90°, translations by column vectors, and combinations of these.

concepts.name: Enlargement
concepts.description: Drawing and fully describing enlargements about a centre with positive, fractional and (Cambridge Extended, ZIMSEC) negative scale factors, and the effect on lengths and areas.

concepts.name: Stretches and shears
concepts.description: One-way and two-way stretches and shears with an axis as the invariant line, their stretch or shear factors, and their effect on area (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Vectors in two dimensions
concepts.description: Vector notation (column vectors, directed line segments, bold letters), equal and negative vectors, addition, subtraction and multiplication by a scalar.

concepts.name: Magnitude of a vector
concepts.description: The magnitude of a column vector, √(x² + y²), and the modulus notation |a|.

concepts.name: Vector geometry
concepts.description: Position vectors, expressing vectors in terms of two given vectors, and using vectors to prove geometrical results such as parallel lines and collinear points, including problems with ratios.

concepts.name: Matrix operations
concepts.description: Matrices as stores of information, the order of a matrix, adding, subtracting and multiplying matrices (products up to 2 × 2), scalar multiplication, and the identity and zero matrices (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Determinant and inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix
concepts.description: The determinant of a 2 × 2 matrix, singular and non-singular matrices, the inverse of a non-singular 2 × 2 matrix, and solving simultaneous linear equations with the inverse matrix (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Matrices and transformations
concepts.description: 2 × 2 matrices for reflections, rotations, enlargements, stretches and shears; finding the matrix of a transformation from the images of points; combined transformations, inverse transformations and area scale factor as the determinant (ZIMSEC).

concepts.name: Basic probability
concepts.description: The language of probability, the probability scale from 0 to 1, the probability of a single event from equally likely outcomes, P(not A) = 1 − P(A), and mutually exclusive outcomes.

concepts.name: Relative and expected frequency
concepts.description: Experimental and theoretical probability, relative frequency as an estimate of probability, fair, biased and random, and expected frequency of outcomes.

concepts.name: Combined events
concepts.description: Sample space diagrams (outcome tables), two-way tables and Venn diagrams for two events, the addition rule for mutually exclusive events and the multiplication rule for independent events.

concepts.name: Tree diagrams
concepts.description: Tree diagrams for two or three events with replacement and (Cambridge Extended, ZIMSEC) without replacement, and using them to find the probabilities of combined outcomes.

concepts.name: Conditional probability
concepts.description: Conditional probability from tables, tree diagrams and Venn diagrams, without formal notation (Cambridge Extended).

concepts.name: Collecting and classifying data
concepts.description: Types of data (qualitative, quantitative, discrete and continuous), collecting data, tally charts, frequency tables, grouped frequency tables and two-way tables.

concepts.name: Interpreting statistical data
concepts.description: Reading, interpreting and drawing inferences from tables and statistical diagrams, comparing data sets using averages and measures of spread, and recognising the limits of conclusions.

concepts.name: Statistical charts and diagrams
concepts.description: Bar charts (including composite and dual bar charts), pie charts, pictograms, ordered stem-and-leaf diagrams with a key, and simple frequency distributions.

concepts.name: Averages and range
concepts.description: Mean, median, mode and range from lists and ungrouped frequency tables, choosing the most suitable average, and (Cambridge Extended) quartiles and the interquartile range of listed data.

concepts.name: Averages of grouped data
concepts.description: Estimating the mean of grouped data from mid-interval values, the modal class and the class containing the median, and (ZIMSEC) calculating the mean with an assumed mean.

concepts.name: Scatter diagrams
concepts.description: Plotting scatter diagrams, positive, negative and zero correlation, and drawing and using a line of best fit (Cambridge).

concepts.name: Cumulative frequency
concepts.description: Cumulative frequency tables and curves, and estimating the median, quartiles, percentiles, interquartile range and (ZIMSEC) semi-interquartile range from them.

concepts.name: Histograms and frequency polygons
concepts.description: Histograms with equal and unequal class widths, frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, finding frequencies from a histogram, and (ZIMSEC) frequency polygons.
